newsitem.title: CHINA: China province cracks down on pornography, piracy.
newsitem.headline: China province cracks down on pornography, piracy.

text.p: Authorities in south China have found and closed nine illegal compact disc production lines in a week as part of a crackdown on pornography and piracy, officials said on Friday.

Acting on tip-offs from callers to an anti-piracy telephone hotline, authorities in Guangdong province have busted nine production lines since December 14, an official of the State Copyright Administration told Reuters by telephone.
The lines had a combined production capacity of up to 20,000 CDs a day, he said.
The official declined to say how many suspects were arrested or how many CDs were seized.
The People's Daily said people who tipped off authorities about underground CD production lines could receive rewards of up to 300,000 yuan ($36,000).
The hotline has received more than 100 calls since December 11, the official said.
China and the United States went to the brink of a trade war in June over Washington's accusations that Beijing was not doing enough to comabt rampant piracy of intellectual property rights.
